newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Argentina pitches ASEAN-Mercosur free trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Argentina pitches ASEAN-Mercosur free trade pact.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem called on Friday for formal links between the Mercosur trading bloc and ASEAN countries, saying a free trade pact would connect the two fastest growing regions in the world.
Menem said in a speech to business officials in Singapore that steady growth among Mercosur members made it imperative to "try and come to an understanding with ASEAN".

"In the next few years, a free trade area can link ASEAN to Mercosur. This is a proposal coming from Argentina that is becoming a reality little by little," Menem said, adding he planned to present the suggestion at a Mercosur summit next year.

Mercosur groups Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay while the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) links Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Menem said the two groups would be a good fit, since ASEAN's economies were expanding by an average of 7-8 percent annually while Mercosur nations were growing by about 5-6 percent per year.
"The doors are completely open. You may invest freely" in Argentina and the Mercosur trading bloc, Menem said.
Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella told reporters after the speech it was possible a framework agreement between the two groups could be reached in the near future.

"It is quite thinkable that we can develop some sort of framework agreement between the two organisations," he said. Di Tella said the agreement could be to form a free trade pact or to expand cooperation in the investment and finance sectors.
He said Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong expressed interest when Menem proposed establishing a special relationship between ASEAN and Mercosur.
"He thought it was a very tempting idea," he said. "We have to do a lot of work."

Singapore Trade and Industry Minister Lee Yock Suan said in a speech to the business officials that the two economic groups were developing closer ties through meetings between ministers and businessmen.
There would be further meetings and "...we will continue to identify and implement other areas of economic cooperation", he said.
Argentina is also interested in joining the 18-member Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

"Mercosur is now a bi-oceanic organisation," Di Tella said. "The Pacific is of great interest to all the Mercosur countries. The Pacific, which is the greatest growth area in the world, is within our reach and we are very keen in developing that connection."
He said Buenos Aires would work on obtaining observer status in APEC. Chile is an APEC member.
Menem was concluding a week-long tour of southeast Asian countries with a business delegation. He went to ASEAN members Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam and was due to fly home on Friday.
